messages:
santiago: Ran an nsys capture on an 8xA100 run this morning to debug those sporadic p99 spikes. TL;DR: timeline shows 4-8ms gaps between token kernels, followed by a tiny all-reduce and a KV prefetch handshake that looks serialized across pipeline stages.

liam: Can you paste the exact capture command + which model/flags you used? Also a perfetto link would help.

santiago: Command was:

```
nsys profile --trace=cuda,nvtx,nccl --capture-range=kernel --output=mgpu_kv_1959 nsys_cmd
python launcher.py --model redwood-7b --seq 1536 --tp 2 --pp 4 --batcher.max_batch_tokens=16384 --kernel_selector=selector-v2
```

Perfetto link: https://perfetto.dev/trace/XYZ-1959 (private trace) — look at the time window ~00:12:34 where the gaps repeat every ~120ms.

anna: Nice. Do the gaps line up with NCCL allreduce start/end markers or with our KV_CACHE_HANDSHAKE nvtx markers?

santiago: Both, but ordering is interesting: token kernel(s) finish on GPU0..GPU7, then an NVTX marker "KV_HANDSHAKE:start", then a short NCCL allreduce (~600-900us), then another marker "KV_HANDSHAKE:commit". The problem is the CPU-side handshake blocks the next kernel launch on some ranks, so overlap is minimal.

michael: What does the kernel selector choose during those windows? Any slow fallback kernels?

santiago: Yep. Selector-v2 flips between the fused-attn kernel and the fallback fp16 gemm path depending on the active seq length estimate. When we switch kernels, there's ~1ms scheduling overhead + kernel warmup which amplifies the gap. I captured a small flame: fused-attn runs ~0.9ms, fallback ~2.1ms, and the transition introduces another ~0.8ms in overhead.

liam: Interesting. So two contributors: (1) KV handshake serialization and (2) kernel selection thrash. Could be aggravated by batching heuristics (batcher chopping batches at odd boundaries).

anna: Any quick repro that toggles one variable? Like force kernel_selector to always prefer fused-attn or disable KV prefetch?

santiago: I tried forcing fused-attn via env/flag: `KERNEL_SELECTOR_FORCE=fused_attn` — that removed the selector flips and reduced the gaps by ~35%, p99 improved ~12%. Disabling kv prefetch (kv_prefetch_window=0) removes the extra NVTX markers but increases token compute slightly because cache misses spike.

michael: Can we get NCCL timeline overlap numbers? How much of the allreduce overlaps with GPU compute vs idle?

santiago: From the perfetto slice: allreduce overlaps with compute ~20% of its walltime. Most of the allreduce is happening in the idle gaps. So moving the allreduce to be more asynchronous or aggregating it would help.

liam: Two experimental actions then: (A) run a capture with `KERNEL_SELECTOR_FORCE=fused_attn` + normal kv_prefetch to measure delta, (B) run with `kv_prefetch_window=2` and `batcher.max_batch_tokens+=8192` to test batching smoothing. I'll spin 2 reproducer runs.

infra-bot: Started job #ci-mgpu-repro-1960 (8xA100). Artifacts will land in s3://redwood-traces/mgpu/1959/ after completion.

anna: Also add an nsys capture with `--trace=nvtx,nccl,cuda,osrt` and include `--export=timeline.json` so we can overlay NVTX markers in perfetto. Please capture a short 30s window instead of the full run to keep file sizes sane.

liam: One more thought — kernel_selector has a `settle_ms` param that waits before switching kernel strategy (to avoid thrash). What's it set to?

santiago: `kernel_selector_settle_ms=0` in current deploy. Setting it to 5-10ms should prevent flip-flopping for our seq distribution. I'll try 8ms in the next run.

michael: If that helps, we can add a fallback that only switches at safe boundaries (end of beam/response). Also worth testing NCCL 2.16 vs 2.15 — there were micro improvements in stream ordering.

santiago: Plan posted to the issue: https://redwood-internal/issue/ENGRT-2342 — steps, perfetto screenshots, and the before/after numbers. Will upload traces and a short video snippet.

anna: Great. After reproducer runs, can someone try the small patch that makes KV_HANDSHAKE run on a pinned background stream (async) so it doesn't block launches? If that reduces overlap it's probably the right long-term fix.

liam: I'll own the batcher smoothing test and the settle_ms tweak.

michael: I'll test the pinned-background-stream variant on my devboard and try NCCL 2.16.

santiago: Thanks all — will attach traces from infra-bot here once they land. :thumbsup:
